title: Ferroelectricity-modulated asymmetric van der Waals heterostructure for ultralow-power neuromorphic synapse and logic-in-memory operations

paper_content.abstract:
Vertical integration of two-dimensional materials holds tremendous potential for integrated
sensing, memory and computing applications, yet it still confronts challenges such as single device
functionality, limited in-memory logic capability and high power consumption. To address these
issues, we propose an asymmetric van der Waals integration strategy based on an
In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/graphene heterojunction, which integrates five reconfigurable logic gates
(AND, OR, NOT, NOR, and NAND), dual-mode photodetection (~10 fA dark current, a high
responsivity of 89.3 mA/W and a specific detectivity of 1.4 × 10¹¹ Jones), and low-power
neurosynaptic functions (7-bit conductance states, subfemtojoule energy consumption) into a
single device. By virtue of these characteristics, the device enables high-precision image
recognition, simulation of classical Pavlovian conditioning and single-pixel dual-band optical
imaging. This work paves a feasible path for the development of multifunctionally integrated
sensor-memory-computing devices.
paper_content.introduction:
In recent years, the rapid advancement of the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial
intelligence (AI) has placed huge demands on the data processing capabilities of terminal devices1-
8. The traditional von Neumann architecture, characterizEed by its separation of memory and
computing9-12, faces challenges such as the "memRory wall" bottleneck and high power
consumption when processing massive sensory
data1P3-15.
Inspired by the highly efficient and low-
power perception and information processinNg mechanisms in biological systems16-18, the
development of sensing-memory-computinIg integrated devices has become crucial for
overcoming the limitations of convEentional computing and advancing next-generation
neuromorphic computing and artificiaLl vision systems19-21.
Among various candidate mIaterials, 2D layered materials have emerged as an ideal platform
for building next-generation optoelectronic devices due to their electrical and optical properties,
atomic-scale thickness, and exceptional integration potential in the post-Moore era22-26. Notably,
in-memory logic computing devices constructed from 2D heterostructures enable high-speed and
high-precision information processing27-29; photodetectors are capable of mimicking artificial
visual perception, showing significant potential in target recognition and imaging applications30-
32; while photonic synaptic devices can directly convert incident optical signals into synaptic
weight updates, offering a highly attractive in-sensor computing solution for the efficient
integration of visual perception and neuromorphic computing33-36. Although these devices show
great potential within their respective domains, integrating multiple functions into a single device
remains a major challenge.
To address these issues, researchers have begun exploring the use of intrinsic physical
properties of materials (such as ferroelectricity) for functionality control37-39. Among these, 2D
ferroelectric materials (such as α-In₂Se₃) leverage their non-volatile polarization states to
effectively modulate carrier transport behavior and alter the band structure of heterojunctions40-44,
thereby opening new pathways for designing low-power, multifunctional optoelectronic devices25.
Recent theoretical predictions suggest that α-In₂Se₃ and MoS₂ form two type-II band-aligned
heterostructure45, wherein the ferroelectric polarization field of α-In₂Se₃ can effectively tune the
interface barrier and channel conductance, offering flexibility for designing photodetection and
synaptic devices. More importantly, large-scale growth processes for both MoS₂ and α-In₂Se₃ thin
films have been successively demonstrated by relevant research groups, highlighting the
substantial potential of these two materials for practical applications42, 46.
Herein, we develop a dual-terminal In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Gra heterojunction device that
integrates multiple functions, including five classic Boolean logic-in-memory operations, broad-
spectrum photoelectric synaptic plasticity, and photodetection. By leveraging the polarization
modulation of In₂Se₃ to tailor the band alignment at the In₂Se₃/MSoOₓ/MoS₂ interface, the device
exhibits electrically tunable positive and negative photorespSonses, successfully emulating five
fundamental Boolean logic operations—AND, OR, NOTE, NOR, and NAND—within a single
device. Furthermore, through the synergy between In₂Se₃ ferroelectric polarization and defect
engineering in MoOₓ/MoS₂, the device demonstrates dual-mode operation (photoelectric synaptic
and photodetection) across a broad spectrumN from ultraviolet to near-infrared. Under the
photoelectric synaptic mode (low voltage), defect levels in the MoOₓ/MoS₂ channel are activated,
enabling charge trapping/detrapping beEhavior. Combined with polarization modulation from
In₂Se₃, the device achieves over 128 (7-bit) continuous conductance states, operates at a voltage
as low as 1 mV, and consumes only 0.03 fJ per electrical synaptic event and 0.37 fJ per optical
synaptic event. In photodetecTtion mode (0 V bias), benefiting from the interfacial control via In₂Se₃
polarization, the dark current is suppressed to sub-fA levels, while the responsivity reaches 89.3
mA/W at 375 nm and the specific detectivity attains 1.4×10¹¹ Jones at 373 nm. Finally, we
successfully demonstrate that the device achieves high-precision image recognition based on
parallel computing of five reconfigurable logic gates coupled with optoelectronic synapses,
emulates classical Pavlovian associative learning, and enables single-pixel dual-band (visible to
near-infrared) optical imaging. In summary, this work not only presents a multifunctional
integrated device with simple structure, rich functionality, and ultralow power consumption, but
also offers a design strategy leveraging intrinsic properties of 2D ferroelectric materials for in-
sensor computing.

High-precision image recognition

We construct and validate an image recognition system based on the Gra/MoS₂/MoO /In₂Se₃
x
heterojunction device. This system innovatively integrates the analog sensing capability of
photoelectric synapses with the reconfigurable digital processing functions of five Boolean logic
gates (OR, AND, NOT, NAND, NOR), enabling efficient hybrid computing. As illustrated in Fig.
5a, the system workflow is as follows: After the raw image is input, the photoelectric synaptic
layer first processes the optical signal in the analog domain, preliminarily extracting basic image
features such as contours and textures. These features are then fed in parallel into five
reconfigurable logic gate branches for specific and differentiated feature enhancement.
Specifically, the OR gate employs depthwise separable convolution to expand the receptive field,
focusing on extracting the overall contour and spatial structure of the target. The AND gate
enhances and focuses on key details and local features in the image through refined convolution
operations. The NOT gate utilizes a channel attention mechanism to achieve feature inversion and
recalibration, effectively suppressing background interference and improving foreground contrast.
The NAND gate uses dilated convolution to enlarge the rReceptive field while employing smoothing
operations to suppress noise, achieving robust featuPre representation. The NOR gate introduces
spatial attention weights to strengthen the response in the core target area, enabling adaptive focus
on the main subject. The differentiated features output by each logic gate are adaptively weighted
and integrated by an intelligent feature fusion module, ultimately forming a unified feature
representation with stronger discrimiLnative power, which is then fed into a classifier to achieve
high-accuracy and high-robustneCss image recognition. Fig. 5b visually compares the feature
extraction characteristics of the photoelectric synaptic layer and the five logic layers, using an
input cat image as an exRample. Fig. 5c further presents the hybrid feature response heatmap
generated from the outAputs of the photoelectric synaptic layer and the logic layers, demonstrating
the enhanced effect after feature fusion. Fig. 5d shows a comparison of the training recognition
accuracy curves between the single photoelectric synaptic layer and the photoelectric
synaptic/logic hybrid layer on the CIFAR-10 dataset. After 100 training epochs, the hybrid layer
achieves an accuracy of 97.28%, significantly higher than the 91.56% accuracy of the single
photoelectric synaptic layer, highlighting the performance advantage brought by the synergistic
processing of logic gates. Fig. 5e, f display the confusion matrix and accuracy distribution,
respectively, for the photoelectric synaptic/logic hybrid layer in recognizing ten types of objects
(such as airplanes, cars, cats, etc.). The average recognition accuracy remains stable at around 97%,
further verifying the system’s high accuracy and strong generalization capability in multi-category
recognition tasks.
paper_content.methods:
Theoretical calculation. First-principles calculations are performed using the Vienna Ab initio
Simulation Package (VASP) based on density functional theory (DFT). The ion-electron
interactions are treated using the projector augmented wave (PAW) method. The exchange-
correlation potential is described by the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) in the scheme
of Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE). The plane-wave energy cutoff is set to 400 eV. The geometry
optimization is allowed to proceed until the residual forces on the atoms are less than 0.05 eV/Å,
and the energy convergence criterion for the self-consistent loop is set to 10−6 eV. The Brillouin
zone integration is sampled using a Γ-centered k-point mesh with a grid density consistent with a
resolution of 0.05 Å⁻¹. The MoS₂/MoOₓ/In₂Se₃ heterostructures are modeled by stacking the
corresponding layers along the z-direction. To investigate the ferroelectric modulation mechanism,
the polarization states of α-In₂Se₃ (Pup and Pdown) are simulated by adjusting the atomic stacking
sequence. The projected band structures are calculated to identify the orbital contributions of each
layer, and the plane-averaged electrostatic potentials are computed to evaluate the band alignment
and the built-in electric field distribution across the interface.

Device fabrication. During device fabrication, 2D nanosheets are first mechanically exfoliated
from bulk crystals of graphene, MoS₂, and In₂Se₃ using polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The
graphene and MoS₂ nanosheets are then sequentially dry-transferred onto a 300 nm SiO₂/Si
substrate. The resulting graphene/MoS₂ heterostructure is annealed at 300 °C for 2 hours. After
cooling to room temperature, an In₂Se₃ nanosheet is transferred onto the heterostructure. To
enhance the interlayer adhesion and improve the optoelectronic performance, the entire device is
heated at 100 °C for 5 minutes. Finally, electrode patterns are defined over the heterojunction
region using a maskless UV lithography system, followed by the deposition of a 5 nm/25 nm metal
layer via thermal evaporation. The photoresist is lifted off in acetone to obtain the final device.

Sample characterization and optoelectronic measurements. TShe physicochemical properties
and morphology of the devices are characterized using X-rayS photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS,
Thermo Scientific Kα+ system) and atomic force miEcroscopy (AFM, Bruker Icon). All
optoelectronic measurements and synaptic behavior emulation are performed on a probe station
equipped with a semiconductor parameter analyzer (Keithley B1500A), using the
In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Gra heterostructure devicesN. For synaptic performance testing, the devices are
optically excited by laser sources spanning 375–808 nm, with laser frequency and pulse width
modulated by a signal generator. Laser inEtensity is monitored in real time using a power meter.

reviewer_comments.reviewer_1:
Zhi et al presented an asymmetric van der Waals heterostructure, In2Se3/MoOx/MoS2/Graphene, demonstrating multifunctional electrical operations, including Boolean logic-in-memory, broad-spectrum photoelectric synaptic plasticity, and photodetection. The device emulates classical Pavlovian conditioning and supports single-pixel dual-band optical imaging. However, although this progress is important, the underlying material platform (In2Se3 and MoS2 ) iand the general concept of van der Waals heterostructures for neuromorphic computing are well-established. Given the lack of significant material or architecture innovation and the preliminary nature of key demonstrations, the reviewer cannot recommend this for publication in a such high impact journal. Some comments are noted as follows.
1.The ferroelectric polarization of α-In2Se3 is critical for achieving device functionality. The authors should provide additional details on the in-situ testing of ferroelectric properties of the α-InSe film. Additionally, there appears to be a serious mismatch between the figure labels and the descriptive text/captions in Fig. 1. Carefully review and revise Fig.1 and its caption to ensure a precise, one-to-one correspondence between the panels.
2.The author mentions that the device exhibits different states before and after annealing. What is the precise mechanism responsible for the state difference before and after annealing? This requires direct, supporting evidence (e.g., XPS spectra comparing the interface before and after annealing, or TEM cross-sections). While the presence of MoOx in annealed MoS2 is noted (Fig. 1g), the authors fail to elaborate on its functional role. Given that MoOx can modify the work function, the authors must discuss how this oxidized layer tunes the band alignment at the InSe/MoS2 interface and consequently regulates device performance (e.g., affects charge transfer or the internal electric field).
3.Reliability data is mandatory for the memory device claim. Please supplement the endurance and retention data of the van der Waals heterostructure. The statement regarding the "working voltage of 1 mV" is confusing and likely refers only to the read operation.
4.Figure 1g shows an α-In2Se3 coercive voltage of approximately 5 V. However, the subsequent memory testing (Fig. 2) is performed using biases significantly lower than 5 V. Since the applied voltage is insufficient to reverse the ferroelectric polarization as determined by the authors' own data, the observed memory window in Fig. 2 cannot be solely due to ferroelectric polarization reversal.
5.The claim of exhibiting "more than 128 (7-bit) continuously tunable conductance states" (Fig. 4g) is excellent, but requires more rigorous support. The authors must explicitly demonstrate the reliability and separation of these 128+ states. This typically involves plotting the distribution of the states to confirm that the noise margin is sufficient to prevent state overlap.
6.The simultaneous demonstration of Boolean logic and analog synapse functionality in a single device is a valuable finding that should be leveraged into a compelling application scenario. The authors should propose a distinctive hybrid application that specifically utilizes the co-existence of both features.
7.The figures must be revised to meet publication quality standards. The "pA" values in Fig.3b are completely illegible. These must be increased in font size and contrast to clearly display the data range. Ensure consistent font style and size across all panels.

reviewer_comments.reviewer_3:
This manuscript reports an asymmetric van der Waals heterostructure (In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Graphene) that integrates multiple functionalities including reconfigurable logic, ultralow-power synaptic behavior, and high-sensitivity photodetection. The key operating principle lies in the active modulation of interfacial band alignment and carrier transport through the ferroelectric polarization of α-In₂Se₃. The novelty of this work is that all three functions—(1) reconfigurable logic, (2) ultralow-power synapse, and (3) broadband photodetection—are demonstrated within a single two-terminal device. While most prior studies on 2D materials have focused on only one of these functionalities, this work achieves their coexistence and interaction within a unified heterostructure, thereby advancing toward the ultimate goal of in-sensor computing and logic-in-memory architectures. The dual-mechanism operation—combining nonvolatile ferroelectric polarization switching in In₂Se₃ with defect-assisted charge trapping/detrapping in MoS₂ introduced by thermal treatment at 300 °C—represents a distinctive and synergistic device design strategy. The results are experimentally elegant and technically intriguing. However, several aspects require further clarification and strengthening:
1. The central operation relies on the synergy between the ferroelectric polarization of In₂Se₃ and the defect states in MoS₂, but the manuscript lacks a quantitative analysis of how these two factors interact. Specifically, it remains unclear how the polarization direction modifies the trapping/detrapping efficiency or the capture cross-section of defect states at the MoOₓ/MoS₂ interface. A more detailed physical discussion supported by band diagram simulations, temperature-dependent measurements, or capacitance-based analyses would substantially enhance the scientific rigor of the paper.
2. All devices are fabricated by mechanical exfoliation, which, although effective for proof-of-concept studies, inherently suffers from device-to-device variation and scalability limitations. To strengthen the validity of the conclusions, statistical data from at least 5–10 devices should be presented for key parameters such as synaptic energy consumption, logic current contrast, and dark current. Furthermore, a brief discussion on the feasibility of wafer-scale or CVD-based fabrication would provide valuable perspective for potential practical implementation.
3. For neuromorphic and memory-oriented devices, endurance (number of polarization or weight-update cycles) and data retention are crucial performance metrics. The manuscript should include endurance tests for both ferroelectric switching and synaptic weight updates, as well as retention measurements showing how long the programmed conductance states can be maintained under ambient conditions.
4. As shown in Fig. 3, the Boolean logic operations depend on current polarity differences at the picoampere level. Such small current windows may be easily affected by noise, temperature fluctuation, or readout uncertainty. The authors should evaluate the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the readout current and verify logic stability under varying bias and temperature conditions. Demonstrating consistent logic output across a range of operating environments would greatly strengthen the practical significance of the results.

## Abstract

Vertical integration of two-dimensional materials holds tremendous potential for integrated
sensing, memory and computing applications, yet it still confronts challenges such as single device
functionality, limited in-memory logic capability and high power consumption. To address these
issues, we propose an asymmetric van der Waals integration strategy based on an
In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/graphene heterojunction, which integrates five reconfigurable logic gates
(AND, OR, NOT, NOR, and NAND), dual-mode photodetection (~10 fA dark current, a high
responsivity of 89.3 mA/W and a specific detectivity of 1.4 × 10¹¹ Jones), and low-power
neurosynaptic functions (7-bit conductance states, subfemtojoule energy consumption) into a
single device. By virtue of these characteristics, the device enables high-precision image
recognition, simulation of classical Pavlovian conditioning and single-pixel dual-band optical
imaging. This work paves a feasible path for the development of multifunctionally integrated
sensor-memory-computing devices.

---

## Introduction

In recent years, the rapid advancement of the Internet of Things (IoT) and artificial
intelligence (AI) has placed huge demands on the data processing capabilities of terminal devices1-
8. The traditional von Neumann architecture, characterizEed by its separation of memory and
computing9-12, faces challenges such as the "memRory wall" bottleneck and high power
consumption when processing massive sensory
data1P3-15.
Inspired by the highly efficient and low-
power perception and information processinNg mechanisms in biological systems16-18, the
development of sensing-memory-computinIg integrated devices has become crucial for
overcoming the limitations of convEentional computing and advancing next-generation
neuromorphic computing and artificiaLl vision systems19-21.
Among various candidate mIaterials, 2D layered materials have emerged as an ideal platform
for building next-generation optoelectronic devices due to their electrical and optical properties,
atomic-scale thickness, and exceptional integration potential in the post-Moore era22-26. Notably,
in-memory logic computing devices constructed from 2D heterostructures enable high-speed and
high-precision information processing27-29; photodetectors are capable of mimicking artificial
visual perception, showing significant potential in target recognition and imaging applications30-
32; while photonic synaptic devices can directly convert incident optical signals into synaptic
weight updates, offering a highly attractive in-sensor computing solution for the efficient
integration of visual perception and neuromorphic computing33-36. Although these devices show
great potential within their respective domains, integrating multiple functions into a single device
remains a major challenge.
To address these issues, researchers have begun exploring the use of intrinsic physical
properties of materials (such as ferroelectricity) for functionality control37-39. Among these, 2D
ferroelectric materials (such as α-In₂Se₃) leverage their non-volatile polarization states to
effectively modulate carrier transport behavior and alter the band structure of heterojunctions40-44,
thereby opening new pathways for designing low-power, multifunctional optoelectronic devices25.
Recent theoretical predictions suggest that α-In₂Se₃ and MoS₂ form two type-II band-aligned
heterostructure45, wherein the ferroelectric polarization field of α-In₂Se₃ can effectively tune the
interface barrier and channel conductance, offering flexibility for designing photodetection and
synaptic devices. More importantly, large-scale growth processes for both MoS₂ and α-In₂Se₃ thin
films have been successively demonstrated by relevant research groups, highlighting the
substantial potential of these two materials for practical applications42, 46.
Herein, we develop a dual-terminal In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Gra heterojunction device that
integrates multiple functions, including five classic Boolean logic-in-memory operations, broad-
spectrum photoelectric synaptic plasticity, and photodetection. By leveraging the polarization
modulation of In₂Se₃ to tailor the band alignment at the In₂Se₃/MSoOₓ/MoS₂ interface, the device
exhibits electrically tunable positive and negative photorespSonses, successfully emulating five
fundamental Boolean logic operations—AND, OR, NOTE, NOR, and NAND—within a single
device. Furthermore, through the synergy between In₂Se₃ ferroelectric polarization and defect
engineering in MoOₓ/MoS₂, the device demonstrates dual-mode operation (photoelectric synaptic
and photodetection) across a broad spectrumN from ultraviolet to near-infrared. Under the
photoelectric synaptic mode (low voltage), defect levels in the MoOₓ/MoS₂ channel are activated,
enabling charge trapping/detrapping beEhavior. Combined with polarization modulation from
In₂Se₃, the device achieves over 128 (7-bit) continuous conductance states, operates at a voltage
as low as 1 mV, and consumes only 0.03 fJ per electrical synaptic event and 0.37 fJ per optical
synaptic event. In photodetecTtion mode (0 V bias), benefiting from the interfacial control via In₂Se₃
polarization, the dark current is suppressed to sub-fA levels, while the responsivity reaches 89.3
mA/W at 375 nm and the specific detectivity attains 1.4×10¹¹ Jones at 373 nm. Finally, we
successfully demonstrate that the device achieves high-precision image recognition based on
parallel computing of five reconfigurable logic gates coupled with optoelectronic synapses,
emulates classical Pavlovian associative learning, and enables single-pixel dual-band (visible to
near-infrared) optical imaging. In summary, this work not only presents a multifunctional
integrated device with simple structure, rich functionality, and ultralow power consumption, but
also offers a design strategy leveraging intrinsic properties of 2D ferroelectric materials for in-
sensor computing.

## Methods

Theoretical calculation. First-principles calculations are performed using the Vienna Ab initio
Simulation Package (VASP) based on density functional theory (DFT). The ion-electron
interactions are treated using the projector augmented wave (PAW) method. The exchange-
correlation potential is described by the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) in the scheme
of Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE). The plane-wave energy cutoff is set to 400 eV. The geometry
optimization is allowed to proceed until the residual forces on the atoms are less than 0.05 eV/Å,
and the energy convergence criterion for the self-consistent loop is set to 10−6 eV. The Brillouin
zone integration is sampled using a Γ-centered k-point mesh with a grid density consistent with a
resolution of 0.05 Å⁻¹. The MoS₂/MoOₓ/In₂Se₃ heterostructures are modeled by stacking the
corresponding layers along the z-direction. To investigate the ferroelectric modulation mechanism,
the polarization states of α-In₂Se₃ (Pup and Pdown) are simulated by adjusting the atomic stacking
sequence. The projected band structures are calculated to identify the orbital contributions of each
layer, and the plane-averaged electrostatic potentials are computed to evaluate the band alignment
and the built-in electric field distribution across the interface.

Device fabrication. During device fabrication, 2D nanosheets are first mechanically exfoliated
from bulk crystals of graphene, MoS₂, and In₂Se₃ using polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The
graphene and MoS₂ nanosheets are then sequentially dry-transferred onto a 300 nm SiO₂/Si
substrate. The resulting graphene/MoS₂ heterostructure is annealed at 300 °C for 2 hours. After
cooling to room temperature, an In₂Se₃ nanosheet is transferred onto the heterostructure. To
enhance the interlayer adhesion and improve the optoelectronic performance, the entire device is
heated at 100 °C for 5 minutes. Finally, electrode patterns are defined over the heterojunction
region using a maskless UV lithography system, followed by the deposition of a 5 nm/25 nm metal
layer via thermal evaporation. The photoresist is lifted off in acetone to obtain the final device.

Sample characterization and optoelectronic measurements. TShe physicochemical properties
and morphology of the devices are characterized using X-rayS photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS,
Thermo Scientific Kα+ system) and atomic force miEcroscopy (AFM, Bruker Icon). All
optoelectronic measurements and synaptic behavior emulation are performed on a probe station
equipped with a semiconductor parameter analyzer (Keithley B1500A), using the
In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Gra heterostructure devicesN. For synaptic performance testing, the devices are
optically excited by laser sources spanning 375–808 nm, with laser frequency and pulse width
modulated by a signal generator. Laser inEtensity is monitored in real time using a power meter.

### Reviewer 1

Zhi et al presented an asymmetric van der Waals heterostructure, In2Se3/MoOx/MoS2/Graphene, demonstrating multifunctional electrical operations, including Boolean logic-in-memory, broad-spectrum photoelectric synaptic plasticity, and photodetection. The device emulates classical Pavlovian conditioning and supports single-pixel dual-band optical imaging. However, although this progress is important, the underlying material platform (In2Se3 and MoS2 ) iand the general concept of van der Waals heterostructures for neuromorphic computing are well-established. Given the lack of significant material or architecture innovation and the preliminary nature of key demonstrations, the reviewer cannot recommend this for publication in a such high impact journal. Some comments are noted as follows.
1.The ferroelectric polarization of α-In2Se3 is critical for achieving device functionality. The authors should provide additional details on the in-situ testing of ferroelectric properties of the α-InSe film. Additionally, there appears to be a serious mismatch between the figure labels and the descriptive text/captions in Fig. 1. Carefully review and revise Fig.1 and its caption to ensure a precise, one-to-one correspondence between the panels.
2.The author mentions that the device exhibits different states before and after annealing. What is the precise mechanism responsible for the state difference before and after annealing? This requires direct, supporting evidence (e.g., XPS spectra comparing the interface before and after annealing, or TEM cross-sections). While the presence of MoOx in annealed MoS2 is noted (Fig. 1g), the authors fail to elaborate on its functional role. Given that MoOx can modify the work function, the authors must discuss how this oxidized layer tunes the band alignment at the InSe/MoS2 interface and consequently regulates device performance (e.g., affects charge transfer or the internal electric field).
3.Reliability data is mandatory for the memory device claim. Please supplement the endurance and retention data of the van der Waals heterostructure. The statement regarding the "working voltage of 1 mV" is confusing and likely refers only to the read operation.
4.Figure 1g shows an α-In2Se3 coercive voltage of approximately 5 V. However, the subsequent memory testing (Fig. 2) is performed using biases significantly lower than 5 V. Since the applied voltage is insufficient to reverse the ferroelectric polarization as determined by the authors' own data, the observed memory window in Fig. 2 cannot be solely due to ferroelectric polarization reversal.
5.The claim of exhibiting "more than 128 (7-bit) continuously tunable conductance states" (Fig. 4g) is excellent, but requires more rigorous support. The authors must explicitly demonstrate the reliability and separation of these 128+ states. This typically involves plotting the distribution of the states to confirm that the noise margin is sufficient to prevent state overlap.
6.The simultaneous demonstration of Boolean logic and analog synapse functionality in a single device is a valuable finding that should be leveraged into a compelling application scenario. The authors should propose a distinctive hybrid application that specifically utilizes the co-existence of both features.
7.The figures must be revised to meet publication quality standards. The "pA" values in Fig.3b are completely illegible. These must be increased in font size and contrast to clearly display the data range. Ensure consistent font style and size across all panels.

### Reviewer 3

This manuscript reports an asymmetric van der Waals heterostructure (In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Graphene) that integrates multiple functionalities including reconfigurable logic, ultralow-power synaptic behavior, and high-sensitivity photodetection. The key operating principle lies in the active modulation of interfacial band alignment and carrier transport through the ferroelectric polarization of α-In₂Se₃. The novelty of this work is that all three functions—(1) reconfigurable logic, (2) ultralow-power synapse, and (3) broadband photodetection—are demonstrated within a single two-terminal device. While most prior studies on 2D materials have focused on only one of these functionalities, this work achieves their coexistence and interaction within a unified heterostructure, thereby advancing toward the ultimate goal of in-sensor computing and logic-in-memory architectures. The dual-mechanism operation—combining nonvolatile ferroelectric polarization switching in In₂Se₃ with defect-assisted charge trapping/detrapping in MoS₂ introduced by thermal treatment at 300 °C—represents a distinctive and synergistic device design strategy. The results are experimentally elegant and technically intriguing. However, several aspects require further clarification and strengthening:
1. The central operation relies on the synergy between the ferroelectric polarization of In₂Se₃ and the defect states in MoS₂, but the manuscript lacks a quantitative analysis of how these two factors interact. Specifically, it remains unclear how the polarization direction modifies the trapping/detrapping efficiency or the capture cross-section of defect states at the MoOₓ/MoS₂ interface. A more detailed physical discussion supported by band diagram simulations, temperature-dependent measurements, or capacitance-based analyses would substantially enhance the scientific rigor of the paper.
2. All devices are fabricated by mechanical exfoliation, which, although effective for proof-of-concept studies, inherently suffers from device-to-device variation and scalability limitations. To strengthen the validity of the conclusions, statistical data from at least 5–10 devices should be presented for key parameters such as synaptic energy consumption, logic current contrast, and dark current. Furthermore, a brief discussion on the feasibility of wafer-scale or CVD-based fabrication would provide valuable perspective for potential practical implementation.
3. For neuromorphic and memory-oriented devices, endurance (number of polarization or weight-update cycles) and data retention are crucial performance metrics. The manuscript should include endurance tests for both ferroelectric switching and synaptic weight updates, as well as retention measurements showing how long the programmed conductance states can be maintained under ambient conditions.
4. As shown in Fig. 3, the Boolean logic operations depend on current polarity differences at the picoampere level. Such small current windows may be easily affected by noise, temperature fluctuation, or readout uncertainty. The authors should evaluate the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the readout current and verify logic stability under varying bias and temperature conditions. Demonstrating consistent logic output across a range of operating environments would greatly strengthen the practical significance of the results.

## Methods

Theoretical calculation. First-principles calculations are performed using the Vienna Ab initio
Simulation Package (VASP) based on density functional theory (DFT). The ion-electron
interactions are treated using the projector augmented wave (PAW) method. The exchange-
correlation potential is described by the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) in the scheme
of Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE). The plane-wave energy cutoff is set to 400 eV. The geometry
optimization is allowed to proceed until the residual forces on the atoms are less than 0.05 eV/Å,
and the energy convergence criterion for the self-consistent loop is set to 10−6 eV. The Brillouin
zone integration is sampled using a Γ-centered k-point mesh with a grid density consistent with a
resolution of 0.05 Å⁻¹. The MoS₂/MoOₓ/In₂Se₃ heterostructures are modeled by stacking the
corresponding layers along the z-direction. To investigate the ferroelectric modulation mechanism,
the polarization states of α-In₂Se₃ (Pup and Pdown) are simulated by adjusting the atomic stacking
sequence. The projected band structures are calculated to identify the orbital contributions of each
layer, and the plane-averaged electrostatic potentials are computed to evaluate the band alignment
and the built-in electric field distribution across the interface.

Device fabrication. During device fabrication, 2D nanosheets are first mechanically exfoliated
from bulk crystals of graphene, MoS₂, and In₂Se₃ using polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The
graphene and MoS₂ nanosheets are then sequentially dry-transferred onto a 300 nm SiO₂/Si
substrate. The resulting graphene/MoS₂ heterostructure is annealed at 300 °C for 2 hours. After
cooling to room temperature, an In₂Se₃ nanosheet is transferred onto the heterostructure. To
enhance the interlayer adhesion and improve the optoelectronic performance, the entire device is
heated at 100 °C for 5 minutes. Finally, electrode patterns are defined over the heterojunction
region using a maskless UV lithography system, followed by the deposition of a 5 nm/25 nm metal
layer via thermal evaporation. The photoresist is lifted off in acetone to obtain the final device.

and morphology of the devices are characterized using X-rayS photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS,
Thermo Scientific Kα+ system) and atomic force miEcroscopy (AFM, Bruker Icon). All

equipped with a semiconductor parameter analyzer (Keithley B1500A), using the
In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Gra heterostructure devicesN. For synaptic performance testing, the devices are
optically excited by laser sources spanning 375–808 nm, with laser frequency and pulse width
modulated by a signal generator. Laser inEtensity is monitored in real time using a power meter.

The novelty of this work is that all three functions—(1) reconfigurable logic, (2) ultralow-power synapse, and (3) broadband photodetection—are demonstrated within a single two-terminal device. While most prior studies on 2D materials have focused on only one of these functionalities, this work achieves their coexistence and interaction within a unified heterostructure, thereby advancing toward the ultimate goal of in-sensor computing and logic-in-memory architectures. The dual-mechanism operation—combining nonvolatile ferroelectric polarization switching in In₂Se₃ with defect-assisted charge trapping/detrapping in MoS₂ introduced by thermal treatment at 300 °C—represents a distinctive and synergistic device design strategy. The results are experimentally elegant and technically intriguing. However, several aspects require further clarification and strengthening:
1. The central operation relies on the synergy between the ferroelectric polarization of In₂Se₃ and the defect states in MoS₂, but the manuscript lacks a quantitative analysis of how these two factors interact. Specifically, it remains unclear how the polarization direction modifies the trapping/detrapping efficiency or the capture cross-section of defect states at the MoOₓ/MoS₂ interface. A more detailed physical discussion supported by band diagram simulations, temperature-dependent measurements, or capacitance-based analyses would substantially enhance the scientific rigor of the paper.
2. All devices are fabricated by mechanical exfoliation, which, although effective for proof-of-concept studies, inherently suffers from device-to-device variation and scalability limitations. To strengthen the validity of the conclusions, statistical data from at least 5–10 devices should be presented for key parameters such as synaptic energy consumption, logic current contrast, and dark current. Furthermore, a brief discussion on the feasibility of wafer-scale or CVD-based fabrication would provide valuable perspective for potential practical implementation.
3. For neuromorphic and memory-oriented devices, endurance (number of polarization or weight-update cycles) and data retention are crucial performance metrics. The manuscript should include endurance tests for both ferroelectric switching and synaptic weight updates, as well as retention measurements showing how long the programmed conductance states can be maintained under ambient conditions.
4. As shown in Fig. 3, the Boolean logic operations depend on current polarity differences at the picoampere level. Such small current windows may be easily affected by noise, temperature fluctuation, or readout uncertainty. The authors should evaluate the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the readout current and verify logic stability under varying bias and temperature conditions. Demonstrating consistent logic output across a range of operating environments would greatly strengthen the practical significance of the results.

## Methods

Theoretical calculation. First-principles calculations are performed using the Vienna Ab initio
Simulation Package (VASP) based on density functional theory (DFT). The ion-electron
interactions are treated using the projector augmented wave (PAW) method. The exchange-
correlation potential is described by the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) in the scheme
of Perdew–Burke–Ernzerhof (PBE). The plane-wave energy cutoff is set to 400 eV. The geometry
optimization is allowed to proceed until the residual forces on the atoms are less than 0.05 eV/Å,
and the energy convergence criterion for the self-consistent loop is set to 10−6 eV. The Brillouin
zone integration is sampled using a Γ-centered k-point mesh with a grid density consistent with a
resolution of 0.05 Å⁻¹. The MoS₂/MoOₓ/In₂Se₃ heterostructures are modeled by stacking the
corresponding layers along the z-direction. To investigate the ferroelectric modulation mechanism,
the polarization states of α-In₂Se₃ (Pup and Pdown) are simulated by adjusting the atomic stacking
sequence. The projected band structures are calculated to identify the orbital contributions of each
layer, and the plane-averaged electrostatic potentials are computed to evaluate the band alignment
and the built-in electric field distribution across the interface.

Device fabrication. During device fabrication, 2D nanosheets are first mechanically exfoliated
from bulk crystals of graphene, MoS₂, and In₂Se₃ using polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS). The
graphene and MoS₂ nanosheets are then sequentially dry-transferred onto a 300 nm SiO₂/Si
substrate. The resulting graphene/MoS₂ heterostructure is annealed at 300 °C for 2 hours. After
cooling to room temperature, an In₂Se₃ nanosheet is transferred onto the heterostructure. To
enhance the interlayer adhesion and improve the optoelectronic performance, the entire device is
heated at 100 °C for 5 minutes. Finally, electrode patterns are defined over the heterojunction
region using a maskless UV lithography system, followed by the deposition of a 5 nm/25 nm metal
layer via thermal evaporation. The photoresist is lifted off in acetone to obtain the final device.

and morphology of the devices are characterized using X-rayS photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS,
Thermo Scientific Kα+ system) and atomic force miEcroscopy (AFM, Bruker Icon). All
optoelectronic measurements and synaptic behavior emulation are performed on a probe station
equipped with a semiconductor parameter analyzer (Keithley B1500A), using the
In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Gra heterostructure devicesN. For synaptic performance testing, the devices are

### Reviewer 1

Zhi et al presented an asymmetric van der Waals heterostructure, In2Se3/MoOx/MoS2/Graphene, demonstrating multifunctional electrical operations, including Boolean logic-in-memory, broad-spectrum photoelectric synaptic plasticity, and photodetection. The device emulates classical Pavlovian conditioning and supports single-pixel dual-band optical imaging. However, although this progress is important, the underlying material platform (In2Se3 and MoS2 ) iand the general concept of van der Waals heterostructures for neuromorphic computing are well-established. Given the lack of significant material or architecture innovation and the preliminary nature of key demonstrations, the reviewer cannot recommend this for publication in a such high impact journal. Some comments are noted as follows.
1.The ferroelectric polarization of α-In2Se3 is critical for achieving device functionality. The authors should provide additional details on the in-situ testing of ferroelectric properties of the α-InSe film. Additionally, there appears to be a serious mismatch between the figure labels and the descriptive text/captions in Fig. 1. Carefully review and revise Fig.1 and its caption to ensure a precise, one-to-one correspondence between the panels.
2.The author mentions that the device exhibits different states before and after annealing. What is the precise mechanism responsible for the state difference before and after annealing? While the presence of MoOx in annealed MoS2 is noted (Fig. 1g), the authors fail to elaborate on its functional role. Given that MoOx can modify the work function, the authors must discuss how this oxidized layer tunes the band alignment at the InSe/MoS2 interface and consequently regulates device performance (e.g., affects charge transfer or the internal electric field).
3.Reliability data is mandatory for the memory device claim. Please supplement the endurance and retention data of the van der Waals heterostructure. The statement regarding the "working voltage of 1 mV" is confusing and likely refers only to the read operation.

This manuscript reports an asymmetric van der Waals heterostructure (In₂Se₃/MoOₓ/MoS₂/Graphene) that integrates multiple functionalities including reconfigurable logic, ultralow-power synaptic behavior, and high-sensitivity photodetection. The key operating principle lies in the active modulation of interfacial band alignment and carrier transport through the ferroelectric polarization of α-In₂Se₃. The novelty of this work is that all three functions—(1) reconfigurable logic, (2) ultralow-power synapse, and (3) broadband photodetection—are demonstrated within a single two-terminal device. While most prior studies on 2D materials have focused on only one of these functionalities, this work achieves their coexistence and interaction within a unified heterostructure, thereby advancing toward the ultimate goal of in-sensor computing and logic-in-memory architectures. The dual-mechanism operation—combining nonvolatile ferroelectric polarization switching in In₂Se₃ with defect-assisted charge trapping/detrapping in MoS₂ introduced by thermal treatment at 300 °C—represents a distinctive and synergistic device design strategy. The results are experimentally elegant and technically intriguing. However, several aspects require further clarification and strengthening:
1. The central operation relies on the synergy between the ferroelectric polarization of In₂Se₃ and the defect states in MoS₂, but the manuscript lacks a quantitative analysis of how these two factors interact. Specifically, it remains unclear how the polarization direction modifies the trapping/detrapping efficiency or the capture cross-section of defect states at the MoOₓ/MoS₂ interface. A more detailed physical discussion supported by band diagram simulations, temperature-dependent measurements, or capacitance-based analyses would substantially enhance the scientific rigor of the paper.
2. All devices are fabricated by mechanical exfoliation, which, although effective for proof-of-concept studies, inherently suffers from device-to-device variation and scalability limitations. To strengthen the validity of the conclusions, statistical data from at least 5–10 devices should be presented for key parameters such as synaptic energy consumption, logic current contrast, and dark current. Furthermore, a brief discussion on the feasibility of wafer-scale or CVD-based fabrication would provide valuable perspective for potential practical implementation.
3. For neuromorphic and memory-oriented devices, endurance (number of polarization or weight-update cycles) and data retention are crucial performance metrics. The manuscript should include endurance tests for both ferroelectric switching and synaptic weight updates, as well as retention measurements showing how long the programmed conductance states can be maintained under ambient conditions.

Such small current windows may be easily affected by noise, temperature fluctuation, or readout uncertainty. The authors should evaluate the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the readout current and verify logic stability under varying bias and temperature conditions. Demonstrating consistent logic output across a range of operating environments would greatly strengthen the practical significance of the results.
